Description.Scope of Services:
The City of Burlingame wishes to establish a contractual relationship to provide paving services on an as-needed basis. The paving services to be provided, includes but it not limited to, for asphalt concrete (AC) and Portland cement concrete (PCC) pavement repair at various locations within the City right-of-way. The contract is for “as-needed services” and is not a guarantee that the City will contact you to perform such services.

The awarded contract will be valid until June 30, 2026 with two 1-year renewal options (commencing on July 1st) at the election of the City. Total charges under this contract are not to exceed $75,000.

The City reserves the right to award multiple contracts in order to meet its operational needs.

Contractor shall meet the following requirements if awarded the contract:

• Must have an active Class A license issued by the Contractors State License Board.
• Must meet the insurance and licensing requirements outlined in the City of Burlingame Contractor Requirements.
• Contractor must be able to meet the requirements in the attached sample agreement and scope of work if awarded the contract.
• Prevailing wage rates must be paid for all work associated with this project.
• The City of Burlingame recognizes that prevailing wage increases may occur during the term of the contract, and consequently will allow labor rate increases of up to 5 percent per year to ensure that the labor rates reflect the current prevailing wage.

Bid Detail.Project Title: As-Needed Recoating Services for Water Division
Bid Detail.License Requirements: Must have an active C-33 license issued by the California Contractors State License Board.
Bid Detail.Project Duration: The length of the contract is upon execution until June 30, 2028 with two 1-year renewal options at the discretion of the City.

Description.Scope of Services:
The City of Burlingame wishes to establish a contractual relationship to provide recoating services and materials on an on-call basis when needed by the City. Specifically, we are inviting companies to provide their hourly labor rates (regular and overtime, prevailing wage) for as-needed recoating services to recoat piping, motors, and appurtenances as directed by the Water Division.

The length of the contract is upon execution until June 30, 2028 with two 1-year renewal options at the discretion of the City. Services under this contract are not to exceed $25,000 per fiscal year. The contract is for “on-call services as-needed” and is not a guarantee that the City will contact you to perform these services.

The City reserves the right to award multiple contracts in order to meet its operational needs.

Contractor shall meet the following requirements if awarded the contract:

• Must have an active C-33 license issued by the California Contractors State License Board.
• Must pay prevailing wages and meet the City’s insurance and business license requirements before starting work. See Sample Agreement and “City of Burlingame Contractor Requirements” for more details.
• The City of Burlingame recognizes that prevailing wage increases may occur during the term of the contract, and consequently will allow labor rate increases of up to 5 percent per year to ensure that the labor rates reflect the current prevailing wage.

Description.Scope of Services:
The work includes, but is not limited to, all labor and equipment to repair, replace, adjust, and maintain pumps, motors, and related mechanical systems; inspection; testing; and emergency response. The Contractor must be able to respond to emergency repairs within 24 hours and to non-emergency repairs within 48 hours. The contract is for “as-needed services” and is not a guarantee that the City will contact you to perform such services. The awarded contract will be valid until June 30, 2026. Total charges under this contract are not to exceed $75,000. The City reserves the right to award multiple contracts in order to meet its operational needs. See Attachment A for additional scope details.
Contractor shall meet the following requirements if awarded the contract:
• The contractor shall possess a Class C-61/D21 (Machinery and Pumps), C-36 and/or C-10 license issued by the Contractors State License Board prior to submitting a proposal. Contractor must provide the City with proof of the license when submitting their proposal.

• Must meet the insurance and licensing requirements outlined in the City of Burlingame Contractor Requirements.

• Contractor must be able to meet the requirements in the attached sample agreement and scope of work if awarded the contract.

• Prevailing wage rates must be paid for all work associated with this project. Workers employed in the work must be paid at rates at least equal to the then current prevailing wage scale as determined by the State Director of the Department of Industrial Relations. Contractors and subcontractors are required to be registered with the Department of Industrial Relations prior to submitting a proposal. All contractors and subcontractors will be required to furnish electronic certified payroll records directly to the Department of Industrial Relations.

• The City of Burlingame recognizes that prevailing wage increases may occur during the term of the contract, and consequently will allow labor rate increases of up to 5 percent per year to ensure that the labor rates reflect the current prevailing wage.

Description.Scope of Services:
For the 2025-2026 Large Tree Pruning and Removal, the work consists of tree removal and pruning of eucalyptus trees and other species growing adjacent railroad tracks and Skyline Blvd, Sanchez Avenue, and La Mesa Court.

Contractor shall be responsible for following all OSHA and ANSI regulations for safe and effective tree work. Additionally, contractor shall follow California DOT requirements for traffic control relating to direction of both vehicle and bicycle traffic. All traffic modifications shall be approved by Burlingame Public Works via an approved encroachment permit. Visit https://www.burlingame.org/900/Encroachment-Permit to view and or complete the application. Work hours are limited to weekdays between 8:00 A.M. – 5:00 P.M.
Description.Other Details:
For the 2025-2026 Large Tree Pruning and Removal, the City will be receiving bids for this project via PB System™, a fully automated web-based vendor and bid management system. Prospective bidders should visit https://pbsystem.planetbids.com/portal/46106/portal-home to register, download bid documents, and submit their bid. All bids must be submitted to PB System™ before 2:00 P.M. on Wednesday, November 26, 2025. Bid results will be publicly opened and read at 2:30 P.M. on Wednesday, November 26, 2025. Those submitting a bid will be sent an email with the conference call information for the bid opening. Additionally, the bid results will be displayed in the PB System™ after they are publicly read.

Special Provisions, Specifications and Plans, including prevailing wage rates to be paid in compliance with Section 1773.2 of the California Labor Code and related provisions, may be inspected in the office of the City Engineer during normal working hours at City Hall, 501 Primrose Road, Burlingame, California. Prevailing wage rates are also available for review at the State of California Department of Industrial Relations’ Web site.

A mandatory pre-proposal meeting associated with this project will be held on Wednesday, November 19, 2025, at 10:00 A.M., at the corner of Trousdale Ave. and Skyline Blvd., Burlingame, CA 94010.

Any questions regarding this project should be submitted through the online Q&A feature of PB System™. Questions can be submitted until 12:00 P.M. on Friday, November 21, 2025. Answers will be made available via PB System™.

The Contractor shall possess a C-61/D49 license prior to submitting a bid.

No contractors and subcontractor may be listed on the bid proposal for a public works project unless registered with the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Labor Code section 1725.5 [with limited exceptions from this requirement for bid purposes only under Labor Code section 1771.5(a)].
